A humanoid is a capital good on a scale that changes the constraint. It lengthens production and raises what labor and land can turn out, which is the abundance Elon is pointing at.

A person supplies about 2,000 hours a year. A robot on a 168 hour week supplies about 8,700. His floor of 1 billion within 10 years, priced in the low 10,000s, equals about 4 billion full time equivalents against a world labor force of 3.5 billion. 
The 10 billion at 15 years is an order of magnitude past that. 

Robots building robots still require saving, because energy, materials, and machines have to be bid into that line.
Expected abundance holds for ordinary wants which is what matters for people as consumers. Housing, food, care, and routine medicine get repriced toward energy and materials until a household’s budget stops being what limits them. 

An owner running 100s or 1,000s of agents earns the return on that capital stock, which is also how universal high income shows up as purchasing power. 

Money prices remain the way to allocate whatever is still scarce, that is energy, locations, raw materials. At least in the short term. 

Energy is the binding input, and settling more than one planet adds land, minerals, and generation beyond a single world.

TLDR: (1) More energy. (2) Multiplanetary doesn’t hurt.

Elon Musk explains why Tesla is being extremely careful while scaling Robotaxi

The ambition is massive...but Elon’s priority is making sure they do not hurt anyone

There are roughly 30,000–40,000 automotive deaths every year in the U.S., and most receive almost no national attention

But if a Tesla Robotaxi injures even ONE person, it can instantly become worldwide headline news and regulators could clamp down on the entire operation

So Tesla has to do two things at the same time:

Scale Robotaxi as fast as humanly possible

AND make sure it causes essentially no harm

Elon put it very simply:

“We do not want to injure anyone”

“And ideally...not even run over a pet”

That is the real constraint on Robotaxi right now

And despite being this cautious, the rollout is accelerating fast

Tesla’s authorized Cybercab fleet in Texas has nearly QUADRUPLED in just one month

45 → 169 Cybercabs

And Tesla now has 589 Robotaxi vehicles authorized in Texas when you include 420 Model Ys

Unsupervised Robotaxi miles have also been growing at double-digit rates week after week

So Tesla is not moving slowly

It’s scaling incredibly fast while trying to maintain an insanely high safety bar

That’s the balance Elon is trying to solve
